review_candidates.title: Regional Projects and Partnerships Support Manager, based in Dakar (Link For External Applicants)
review_candidates.description: BACKGROUND ON IMPACT INITIATIVES IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, which include i) the REACH Initiative aimed at facilitating the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision-making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts, ii) the PANDA Initiative aimed at directly supporting key aid actors in improving the effectiveness, efficiency, and efficacy of their programmes, and iii) the AGORA Initiative aimed at promoting localised and multi-sectoral aid action in support of the recovery and stabilisation of crisis-affected communities. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of Acted, and the two organisations have a strong complementarity formalised in a global partnership, enabling IMPACT to benefit from Acted’s operational support in its fields of intervention. Recent funding and access constraints have accelerated a restructuring of our operations. In West and Central Africa, this led to the setup of a Multi-Country Office (MCO) in Dakar, Senegal, where IMPACT holds a registered office and from which it supervises the activities of country missions in the region, through various operating models, increasingly in cooperation with not-for-profit partners. As of today, the MCO in Dakar provides support and oversight to Mali, Niger, Cameroon, Burkina Faso, Benin, Côte d’Ivoire, Mauritania, CAR, Nigeria, Chad and DRC. Some of the functions, including the present one, also provide support to LAC (Haiti). We are currently looking for a Regional Projects and Partnerships Support Manager (RPPSM) to oversee our project development and grant management activities for our missions in West and Central Africa. Title: Regional Projects and Partnerships Support Manager Location: Dakar, Senegal (with travel across West and Central Africa) covering the following countries: Mauritania, Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, Benin, Côte d’Ivoire, Chad, Central African Republic, Nigeria, Cameroon, DRC Contract duration: 12 months Start date: 01 February 2027 COUNTRY PROFILE In addition to the restructuring process outlined above, the humanitarian situations in the region may be interlinked by cross-border dynamics such as the increasing effects of climate change or displacement patterns, and this requires information management actors to adopt a regional approach for a comprehensive overview of the dynamics affecting vulnerable communities. Present in West and Central Africa since 2012, IMPACT currently has missions in Benin/Côte d’Ivoire, Burkina Faso, Central African Republic, Chad, Mali, Niger, Mauritania, Cameroon and Nigeria, implementing REACH and PANDA projects and aiming to develop synergies between them through a regional perspective. Functions Under the management of the HQ PPS Manager, the RPPSM is responsible for supporting the identification, development and management of grants in the countries outlined above, as well as contributing to the development of the IMPACT regional portfolio and representation in the area. The ideal candidate would be eager to work within a dynamic and motivated team and would have a clear focus on project development as a tool to improve the efficacy of the humanitarian response in the region. The priorities will be determined together with the Dakar-based Multi-Country Representative (MCR), the respective Country Representatives (CRs) in the area, as well as the Regional Coordinator (RC) for West Africa (based in Geneva). The RPPSM will have functional management of the country-dedicated Projects and Partnerships Support (PPS) team (at the time of writing, DRC), and direct line management of the pooled PPS Assistant (PPSA), who covers PPS functions for the countries served by the multi-country hub. The RPPSM manages the PPS Department in Dakar, currently composed of one pooled PPSA and one Haiti-dedicated PPS Officer (PPSO). The RPPSM is a decentralised team member of the Projects and Partnerships Support Team based in Geneva. Responsibilities The RPPSM will manage the workflow of the regional hub PPS team, delegating workload appropriately to ensure tasks are carried out, and will proactively identify gaps and overloads and work with the MCR/CRs as well as the Regional Coordinator to ensure these are mitigated. As the role also includes elements formerly handled at HQ level, the RPPSM will also be responsible for specific HQ-delegated tasks (including validation, training and technical backstopping). Support to Positioning and Fundraising All of the tasks below are in support of the MCR and the CRs of the concerned country missions as well as the IMPACT Regional Coordinator, and the RPPSM’s involvement may vary according to the profile, seniority and context. Context Analysis Support the MCR and CRs in analysing the socio-economic situation, donor and funding trends, needs and gaps in the region, with a particular focus on large-scale trends such as climate, as well as regional crises such as the Sahel crisis. Regularly conduct stakeholder analysis for the region, including who does what and where. Alert the MCR, CRs and RC of gaps and emerging needs in order to trigger donor discussions/assessments in a timely manner. Strategy development and Fundraising Contribute to the development of country and regional programme strategies in alignment with IMPACT’s global strategy and roadmap through engagement with external actors, context monitoring, and relevant focal points. Based on the IMPACT strategy, support the identification of regional and, where relevant (with the MCR and pooled PPSO), country-specific funding opportunities and donors to ensure funding continuity and support the diversification of IMPACT’s donor portfolio by tracking funding opportunities and, where relevant, engaging with donors and donor working groups. In line with IMPACT strategy and expertise, contribute to partner mapping to identify potentially relevant international and/or local partners (academia, think tanks, national and international NGOs, private sector partners, etc.) both at regional level and for country-specific cooperation. External Relations In coordination with the CRs and country-dedicated PPSOs, support the overall cooperation with IMPACT’s sister organisation Acted (hosting IMPACT in some of its fields of operation) or other hosting partners, as relevant, in relation to project development and grants management across all countries of focus, ensuring communication is regular and timely and synergies are sought and built. Contribute to establishing, maintaining and improving active and regular working relationships with donors, IMPACT partners, NGOs, UN agencies, relevant working groups, consortia and academia in relation to project implementation and proposal development and, where relevant, act as point of contact for all formal/informal donor communication. Foster IMPACT representation in regional coordination forums in collaboration with regional staff including the IMPACT Regional Coordinator. In coordination with pooled PPSOs and country-dedicated PPSOs, maintain an up-to-date directory of donors, international and local NGOs, other partners and stakeholders. Contribute to setting up a standardised Funding Tracker (or similar tool) across the region, and ensure fundraising activities are tracked in it and updated regularly to log the latest negotiations and proposal possibilities with donors. Grant Management Proposal Development Oversee project proposal conceptualisation (problem statement, logframe), and the development of other fundraising documents (expressions of interest, concept notes) in line with IMPACT country and regional strategy and donor requirements and in close collaboration with partners and finance. Liaise with the HQ PPS team on the submission of any proposal in the region by updating the global Project Cycle Management (PCM) follow-up tool, Ninox. Liaise with the RC, CRs, Research Managers, Operations Manager and other relevant departments to ensure proposals are relevant and technically sound, as well as with other internal stakeholders such as Finance for the budget and other budget-related documents (e.g. budget narrative). Coordinate validation processes with IMPACT HQ PPS for all proposals, new donors and partners. Coordinate timely responses to all donor comments on proposals in liaison with relevant staff in country, IMPACT HQ PPS and Finance teams. Contracting In coordination with the RC, CRs and IMPACT HQ, review/negotiate contracts with donors, ensuring requirements are clear and understood. In coordination with the HQ PPS team, organise the incorporation of contractual elements into the Ninox database. Repeat both steps above for every contract amendment signed during implementation, so that Ninox always reflects the latest contractual terms. Project Implementation and Follow-up Ensure the timely completion of grant-related processes such as monitoring and reviewing project records in Ninox. Ensure timely kick-off meetings are held involving all project components and focal points. Ensure ad hoc requests from donors are addressed in liaison with the CR, Programme and support teams. Implement and oversee the project-specific filing system for grant management and ensure it is regularly updated. Provide ad-hoc support to project implementation through troubleshooting and eliminating blocking points. Reporting Oversee the development of quality project narrative and M&E reports (in support of donors’ requests), reflecting the progress and status of projects in a transparent, timely and professional manner, in liaison with IMPACT HQ PPS and finance. This includes providing capacity building to PPSOs in the region (dedicated and pooled). Validate all donor reports to be submitted in the region from pooled PPSOs and country-dedicated PPSOs, in liaison with CRs and MCR. Liaise with Programme teams when preparing reports, and with Finance to ensure coherence and alignment between financial and narrative reports by cross-checking data between the two. Organise the reporting requirements for a given month in coordination with country-dedicated and pooled PPSOs, and ensure smooth and regular communication with IMPACT HQ PPS, notably by actively flagging any issue or delay that may require additional attention and potential adaptation (e.g. amendment requests or programme adaptations requiring formalisation). Partnerships In close liaison with and under the supervision of the MCR/relevant CRs: In coordination with the HQ PPS team, organise the formalisation of partnerships with IMPACT’s hosting partners in given projects and country missions by following up on the subgrant agreement requirements, ensuring the Ninox database is up to date. Contribute to vetting and due diligence exercises of funding partners in liaison with HQ PPS. Contribute to identifying potential partnerships for providing operational and/or technical support for IMPACT programmes, both for funded and unfunded partnerships. In coordination with HQ PPS and partner’s FLAT departments, facilitate or take part in discussions with implementing partners, including due diligence and vetting, and formalising contractual modalities (outline of contracts). Ensure partners have a clear understanding of IMPACT policies, procedures, compliance, programmatic and financial reporting requirements. Where relevant, review partner reporting regularly and flag any issues in a timely manner to MCR and partner focal points, suggest potential solutions, and act as field point of contact for all formal/informal implementing partner communication. Monitoring and Evaluation Ensure a clear M&E framework for each ongoing project is developed based on project proposals, implementation plans, and donor reporting requirements (including contractual monitoring and evaluation indicators to be tracked as part of activities). review_candidates.title: Zendesk Manager / Developer of Solutions for Migrations into Zendesk (m/f/d)
review_candidates.description: At Flix, we offer a dynamic work environment with competitive pay, strong growth opportunities, and a tech-driven approach to making travel more accessible, sustainable, and affordable. At Flix, Customer Service actively transforms how we provide a service to our passengers while adopting frontier technologies. ZenDesk is one of the systems to be implemented after the pilot and you will own this. As a Zendesk Manager / Developer of Solutions for Migrations into Zendesk , you are the person who does the actual configuration work: you build the workflows, routing, and channel setup that hundreds of agents and millions of passengers will use every day. You sit inside the business team. You take business requirements from market and process owners, turn them into working Zendesk configuration yourself. You own what is shipped in production. You are comfortable being the most hands-on Zendesk person in the room. About The Role Platform configuration: build and maintain the core Zendesk setup across Support, Guide, Talk, and Messaging: ticket fields and forms, groups, views, macros, triggers, automations, SLA policies, omnichannel routing, brands, and roles and permissions. You work in a sandbox-to-production model and keep the instance clean as it grows; config sprawl across 30 markets is a real risk and part of your job is preventing it. Channel setup: configure Voice (Zendesk Talk on Amazon Connect, including IVR and contact flows), email, webform, messaging, and Help Center for each market, in the local language, working from the global blueprint and adapting it where market-specific rules genuinely require it. Rollout delivery: for each market wave, translate the migration plan into configuration - replicate the blueprint, apply market specifics, run test cycles with local teams, support go-live and hypercare, and hand over to steady-state operations. Integrations: configure marketplace apps and webhooks yourself; for custom API integrations into Flix backend systems and AI-driven contact channels (chatbot, voicebot), you define the requirements and test the result while the engineering teams build and own the integration itself. Collaboration: work daily with business SMEs who own rules and processes, the training lead who prepares agents for each go-live, IT engineering who owns integrations and security, and the project lead who owns the rollout plan. Documentation: document all configuration and market-specific deviations to Centre of Excellence standards, so nothing you build depends on you being in the room. About You Zendesk experience: 5+ years hands-on administering and configuring Zendesk in production (we care about proven delivery), on Enterprise plans: triggers, automations, macros, SLA policies, ticket forms, custom fields and objects, and omnichannel routing. You understand trigger firing order, know how to prevent loops, and can explain why a tag taxonomy matters. Zendesk Admin certification is a plus. Scale: you have run or significantly contributed to a Zendesk instance serving multiple brands, markets, or languages, and can talk concretely about what broke as it grew and how you fixed it. Experience migrating from another platform (Salesforce Service Cloud or similar) is a strong plus. Channel breadth: beyond ticketing, you have configured at least two of - Talk or another contact center voice channel (IVR, contact flows), Messaging with bot flows, or a multi-language Help Center (content structure, permissions, theming basics). Integration literacy: you understand how Zendesk talks to other systems (REST APIs, webhooks, OAuth and API keys, JSON payloads). You can read API documentation independently and have a precise conversation with engineers about what an integration should do. Zendesk Apps Framework experience is a plus but not required. Hybrid profile: you thrive in a roughly 70/30 technical-business role: you sit inside the business, gather requirements yourself, push back when a requested workflow will not scale, and explain technical decisions to non-technical stakeholders. Rollout mindset: you are comfortable with repetition done well - the same blueprint deployed market after market, each time tested properly, each deviation documented. Go-lives and hypercare periods do not rattle you. Communication: clear written documentation and communication in English; you leave behind artefacts other people can pick up.
